objectives: Master lighting fundamentals: key/fill/back + motivated practicals.
Survey the modern fixture inventory from tungsten to LED.
Understand color temperature + color spaces + LUTs + DI workflow.

slides.title: Lighting fundamentals: key, fill, back, practical, motivated
slides.body:
**Three-point lighting** — the foundational schematic of cinematic lighting. Three primary light functions:

- **Key light** — the main illuminator of the subject. Sets the direction + character. Hard or soft, high or low, warm or cool.
- **Fill light** — opposite-side filler that reduces shadow contrast. Often a bounce (reflector) or a softbox. Key-to-fill ratio sets contrast: 1:1 flat, 2:1 standard, 4:1 dramatic, 8:1+ low-key noir.
- **Backlight (rim, hair light)** — separates subject from background by lighting the edges from behind. Creates the classic Hollywood glow.

**Other functions**:
- **Background / set light** — illuminates the environment behind/around the subject.
- **Kicker** — a 3/4-back side light that adds dimension.
- **Eye light** — small source close to camera placing a catchlight in the eye.
- **Practical** — a light source within the frame (lamp, candle, neon sign, window) that appears 'real' to the scene.
- **Motivated** — off-screen lighting whose direction + quality is justified by an implied or visible source. Sunlight through a window motivates a hard side key; an overhead practical motivates a soft top key. Motivated lighting is the modern realist default.

**High-key vs low-key**:
- **High-key** — bright, low-contrast, even illumination, soft shadows. Sitcom, comedy, advertising, optimistic dramas.
- **Low-key** — dark, high-contrast, deep shadows, often single source. Film noir, thriller, horror.

**Hard vs soft light**:
- **Hard light** — small + distant source → sharp shadow edges (point-like). Direct sun, bare bulb, tightly focused Fresnel, ARRI M-series HMI. Sculptural, harsh, dramatic.
- **Soft light** — large + close source → diffused shadows (extended source). Overcast sky, large diffusion frame, Kino Flo bank, SkyPanel through a Lite Grid + diffusion. Flattering for faces.

**Chiaroscuro + the painterly tradition**:
- **Caravaggio** (1571-1610) — Italian Baroque master. *The Calling of Saint Matthew*, *Judith Beheading Holofernes*. **Tenebrism** = extreme chiaroscuro with deep blacks + hot specular light. A single off-screen source (often window-like) carves form. Caravaggio's lighting is the conceptual ancestor of film noir + much modern cinematic 'motivated' lighting.
- **Rembrandt** (1606-1669) — *The Night Watch*, *The Anatomy Lesson*. The **Rembrandt lighting pattern**: small triangle of light on the cheek opposite the key, formed by the nose's shadow meeting the cheek shadow. Standard portrait pattern.
- **Vermeer** — soft side-window light. Jack Cardiff explicitly cited Vermeer for *Black Narcissus*.

**Standard lighting patterns on the face**:
- **Paramount / butterfly / glamour** — key directly above + in front of subject. Symmetric butterfly shadow under the nose. Classic Hollywood glamour.
- **Loop** — key slightly off-axis, small nose shadow that loops to the cheek.
- **Rembrandt** — see above; key at 45° + slightly above.
- **Split** — key 90° to one side; half face in light, half in shadow.
- **Short / broad** — key on the far / near side of a turned face; short narrows + broad widens.
- **Beauty dish + ring light** — modern fashion lighting; flat, glamorous, characteristic catchlight.

slides.title: Fixtures: tungsten, HMI, fluorescent, LED — the modern toolkit
slides.body:
**Tungsten** — incandescent halogen lamps at color temperature ~3200 K (warm orange-yellow). Workhorse of classical Hollywood + still used.
- **Mole-Richardson Inkie / Tweenie (650 W) / Baby (1 kW) / Junior (2 kW) / Senior (5 kW) / Tener (10 kW)** — Fresnel lamps in standard sizes.
- **ARRI 650 / 1K / 2K / 10K Fresnel**.
- **Open-face redhead + blonde** — bare-bulb soft sources, 650 W / 2 kW.
- Pros: full continuous spectrum, dimmable without color shift, perfect color rendering. Cons: hot, fragile, power-hungry, fragile filaments.

**HMI (Hydrargyrum Medium-arc Iodide)** — daylight-balanced metal-halide arc lamps at ~5600 K.
- **ARRI M-series (M18, M40, M90)** — modern reflector-based HMIs replacing classic Pars.
- **ARRI / K5600 Joker** + **Briese** + **HMI Par 1.2/2.5/4/6/12/18 kW**.
- Pros: very high output, daylight balanced — match natural sunlight. Cons: requires ballast, slow strike-time, expensive.

**Fluorescent**:
- **Kino Flo** (Frieder Hochheim + Robby Müller invented for *Barfly*, 1987) — banks of high-frequency-ballast fluorescent tubes. Tungsten or daylight tubes. Soft, cool-running, low-power, flicker-free. Sizes: Diva (2-tube), Tegra, Image, ParaBeam, Select LED. Revolutionized location lighting in the 1990s — Müller + Khondji + Doyle all relied heavily on Kinos.

**LED (light-emitting diode)** — dominant since ~2015. Pros: cool, low-power, dimmable, color-tunable in software, often battery-powered.
- **ARRI SkyPanel S30 / S60 / S120 / S360** — the modern industry-standard LED soft panel. Bi-color + RGBW.
- **ARRI Orbiter** — high-output point-source LED with interchangeable optics (Fresnel, Open Face, Projection).
- **Litepanels Gemini + Sola + Astra**.
- **Aputure** (Chinese manufacturer revolutionizing budget cinema lighting) — **Light Storm 600x / 1200d / 1200t**, **Nova P300C / P600C**, **Amaran**, **MC RGB tubes**. High output at lower price points; democratized indie + streaming lighting.
- **Astera Titan Tube + Helios Tube + AX1** — battery-powered pixel-mappable color tubes — set decoration + practicals + lighting effects.
- **Quasar Q-LED + LiteGear LiteMat + Nanlite Forza + Creamsource Vortex** — soft panels + Pars.
- **DMX + RDM + Art-Net + sACN** — networked control protocols making large LED grids programmable.

**Modifiers** — diffusion (216 + 250 + 1/4 grid cloth + Magic Cloth + Ultrabounce), bounce (Ultrabounce, foamcore, beadboard), negative fill (Solid black flag), grids (egg crate snoot), cucoloris ('cookie') casting pattern, gobos (geometric patterns), nets + scrims (cut intensity).

**Power + grip**:
- **Genny / generator** — Honda EU3000, Magnum mobile diesel sets, Tier 4 quiet generators.
- **Distro** — 100A bates connectors → lunchbox / siamese.
- **Grip equipment** — C-stands, combo stands, Matthews, Modern Studio, Avenger, Manfrotto. Cardellini clamps, Mafer clamps, baby pin, junior pin.
- **Truck packages** — 1-ton + 3-ton + 5-ton lighting trucks.

The modern set is a hybrid: tungsten + HMI for hard sources, Kino + LED softboxes for soft fill, Astera tubes for practicals, all dimmable + DMX-controlled.

slides.title: Color: temperature, color spaces, LUTs, DI workflow
slides.body:
**Color temperature** (CCT, correlated color temperature) — the temperature of a Planckian black-body radiator whose color matches the light. Measured in kelvin (K).
- **1700-1900 K** — candle flame.
- **2700-3000 K** — incandescent household bulb.
- **3200 K** — tungsten studio standard.
- **4300 K** — fluorescent cool white.
- **5600 K** — direct noon sunlight + HMI / daylight.
- **6500 K** — overcast sky, D65 monitor white point.
- **10000+ K** — open blue shade.

A white-balanced camera matches its 'white' to the chosen source temperature. Mixing tungsten + daylight without correction yields warm/cool color contrast — used expressively (the orange-and-teal blockbuster look) or balanced via CTO/CTB gels (Color Temperature Orange / Blue).

**Color rendering metrics**:
- **CRI (Color Rendering Index)** — older standard, 0-100, measures rendering of 8 pastel reference colors against blackbody/daylight. CRI > 90 is excellent. Older LEDs (< 2015) often had CRI ~ 80 + dropped on saturated reds — visible on skin.
- **TLCI (Television Lighting Consistency Index)** — newer EBU standard targeting video reproduction. Closer to actual workflow.
- **SSI (Spectral Similarity Index)** — modern; compares full SPDs.
- Modern cinema-grade LEDs (Orbiter, SkyPanel S60-C, Aputure 1200d II) achieve CRI > 95 + TLCI > 90.

**Color spaces**:
- **sRGB / Rec.709** — HD television standard. ~ 35% of visible chromaticities. Default for most online video + television delivery.
- **DCI-P3** — digital cinema projection. Wider gamut, particularly reds. Apple display standard.
- **Rec.2020** — UHD broadcast standard. Much wider gamut, closer to full visible.
- **ACES (Academy Color Encoding System)** — proposed by the Academy as scene-referred color-management standard. ACEScg / ACEScct / ACEScc working spaces; IDTs (Input Device Transforms) for each camera; ODTs (Output Device Transforms) for each delivery; one consistent color-managed pipeline. Adopted widely 2014+.
- **Display referred vs scene referred** — Rec.709 is display-referred (0-1 linear maps to projector light); ACES is scene-referred (0-1+ maps to scene linear light + tone-mapping happens at output).

**Log gamma + LUTs**:
- **Log gamma** (LogC3, LogC4, S-Log3, Log3G10) — encodes 14-17 stops dynamic range into 10-12 bit signal preserving highlight + shadow detail. Log footage is flat + desaturated on a Rec.709 monitor.
- **LUT (Look-Up Table)** — 1D or 3D mapping from one color space to another. **Viewing LUTs** convert log → Rec.709 for monitoring. **Creative LUTs** bake an artistic look (Kodak 2383 print film emulation, ENR, bleach bypass, etc.).
- **CDL (ASC Color Decision List)** — standardized slope/offset/power per channel + saturation. Round-trips on-set creative grading data into DI.

**DI (Digital Intermediate)** — post-production color grading.
- **DaVinci Resolve** (Blackmagic) — dominant DI tool, free version + Studio. Nodes-based grading; primary + secondary corrections; tracking; key-grading; HDR.
- **Baselight (FilmLight)** + **Lustre (Autodesk)** + **NUCODA** — high-end alternatives.
- **Colorists** — distinct guild from cinematographers; partners during finishing. Mitch Paulson, Stefan Sonnenfeld, Tom Poole, Stephen Nakamura.

**Influential DI cinematographers**:
- **Shane Hurlbut, ASC** — wrote extensively about DI workflow; Hurlbut Visuals + Hurlbut Academy education channels.
- **Steve Yedlin, ASC** — has published deeply technical research on color science + Display Prep + texture simulation (yedlin.net) — argues that 'cinema look' is mostly a function of careful display-prep + finishing, not capture format.
- **Steve Bellamy + Mitch Paulson + Yvan Lucas + Stefan Sonnenfeld** — leading colorists.

**The modern color pipeline**: shoot log RAW → on-set LUT (CDL + show LUT) → editorial proxy → final conform → DI grade in ACES or camera-native → output Rec.709 / DCI-P3 / Rec.2020 HDR / Dolby Vision.

question.question: Design a low-key noir lookup with key + fill + practical
question.goal: Subject in 1930s detective office at night. Single window practical + ceiling light off. Build a Caravaggio-influenced low-key lighting plan.

steps.prompt: What motivates the key light? Where do you place it?

acceptedAnswers: the window practical motivates a hard side key from the window direction

steps.reveal: The window practical (a yellow tungsten-bulb desk lamp or sodium street lamp through venetian blinds) motivates a hard side-key from that direction. ARRI M18 HMI (5600 K) through blinds + a CTO gel to bring it to ~3200 K matches the sodium-street motivation. Hard shadows on the opposite wall.

steps.prompt: Choose key-to-fill ratio + the fill source.

acceptedAnswers: 8:1 or 16:1 fill ratio; minimal negative-bounce fill

steps.reveal: Low-key noir: 8:1 or 16:1. Fill is minimal — perhaps a small bounce off the desk surface or a tiny LED panel just opening the eye-side shadows so eyes register. Many shots use no fill at all + let half the face go to black. Caravaggio's *Calling of Saint Matthew* has effectively zero fill — pure tenebrism.

steps.prompt: Where does the backlight come from in noir?

acceptedAnswers: a practical street lamp or window from behind motivates a rim light on the hair and shoulder

steps.reveal: Backlight motivated by another street lamp or office window — Aputure 600d or LED hair-light high + behind. Rim light on the hair + shoulder edges separates the subject from the dark background. Smoke or haze (a hazer + a fan) makes the back rim into volumetric shafts — quintessential noir.

acceptedAnswers: use a cucoloris or actual blinds to throw striped shadows across the subject and wall

steps.reveal: Venetian blinds (real or a 'cookie' / cucoloris cut to simulate) in front of the key throw horizontal striped shadow across face + wall — the iconic noir signifier. Combine with the hazed back light + Caravaggesque chiaroscuro + you have *The Big Combo* (1955, John Alton). Add a desk lamp (practical) + a glowing cigarette + you are in *Sweet Smell of Success* (James Wong Howe, 1957).

question.finalResult:
$$\boxed{\text{Key: hard, motivated; fill: minimal; back: rim + haze; practicals + gobos}}$$

Noir is high-contrast Caravaggesque tenebrism applied to crime drama. Cinematographers John Alton, James Wong Howe, Stanley Cortez, Nicholas Musuraca codified the look in the 1940s-50s.

question.question: What is the Kino Flo + who invented it for which film?
options: An HMI line for daylight exteriors invented for *Apocalypse Now*.

A bank of high-frequency-ballast fluorescent tubes in tungsten- or daylight-balanced versions. Invented by **Frieder Hochheim** + cinematographer **Robby Müller** for Barbet Schroeder's *Barfly* (1987) — Müller needed a soft, cool, low-power source for cramped LA bar interiors that could be hidden in walls + ceilings. The flicker-free ballast (above audible + above shutter rates) was the breakthrough. Kino Flo revolutionized 1990s location lighting — Khondji + Doyle + Müller + virtually every indie-era DP came to depend on Diva / Tegra / Image / ParaBeam fixtures. Modern variants include LED Select. Kino Flo's introduction is one of the most significant fixture innovations of the past 40 years.
question.explanation: Kino Flo = high-frequency-ballast fluorescent tubes invented 1987 by Frieder Hochheim with Robby Müller for *Barfly* (Schroeder). Flicker-free, soft, cool, low-power. Revolutionized 1990s location lighting + remains a workhorse fixture.

slides.workedSolution: Kino Flo — high-frequency-ballast fluorescent tubes, invented 1987 by Frieder Hochheim with DP Robby Müller for *Barfly* (1987). Flicker-free, soft, cool-running, low-power, tungsten or daylight balanced. Revolutionized 1990s location cinematography.

question.question: Why is ACES becoming the industry standard for color management?
question.prompt: A streaming feature shoots with ARRI Alexa 35 (LogC4 ARRIRAW), shoots second-unit with Sony Venice 2 (X-OCN S-Log3), drone with DJI Inspire 3 (DLog-M), and delivers Rec.709 SDR + DCI-P3 PQ HDR + Dolby Vision. Explain how the ACES pipeline (IDT → ACEScg working → ODT) solves the cross-camera + cross-deliverable color-management problem that pre-ACES workflows handled ad-hoc. Reference the Academy's motivation.

question.question: If your tungsten source is **3200 K** + your camera is white-balanced to **5600 K daylight**, in what direction does the recorded tungsten image shift (warmer or cooler)?
question.hint: WB at 5600 expects daylight; tungsten emits more red/yellow.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain how the three-point system + motivated practicals + log-to-ACES color pipeline produce the modern cinematic look.
question.rubric: Mentions: (1) three-point (key + fill + back) is the schematic foundation but modern cinematography uses **motivated** lighting — every off-screen source justified by an implied practical or natural source; (2) practicals (lamps, windows, neon, fire, LED tubes) appear in frame + sell the realism; (3) modern fixtures — ARRI SkyPanel, Aputure 600d, Astera tubes, Kino Flo (Robby Müller / Hochheim 1987) — are bi-color + DMX-controllable + battery-powered, enabling location flexibility; (4) cameras record log gamma (LogC4, S-Log3) preserving 14-17 stops; (5) on-set show LUT + CDL preview the final look; (6) DI in DaVinci Resolve / Baselight in ACES color management round-trips all cameras + deliverables (Rec.709 SDR + DCI-P3 HDR + Dolby Vision); (7) colorists like Stefan Sonnenfeld + Mitch Paulson finalize. Caravaggio + Vermeer ancestors of motivated light still readable in *Skyfall*, *Sicario*, *Roma*, *Oppenheimer*.
